title: Close a 300 mm wafer shipping box in the maker's order: left edge in and latched, right side pressed flush and latched
keywords: door pressed flush against wafer cushion
instruction: Close the wafer shipping box: carry its door by the D-rings, latch its left edge in first, press the right side flush, latch it, fold both rings down.
context: Closing a 300 mm wafer shipping box means pressing a free door flush against a spring-loaded wafer cushion while a latch turns, in a fast-growing industry: SEMI projects 2026 300 mm fab equipment spending at 149 billion USD (up 31%), 227 billion by 2029, and wafer shipments rose 5.8% in 2025 to 12,973 million square inches (SEMI, README). Fab and R&D staff re-pack 300 mm wafers in front-opening shipping boxes (FOSBs) by hand. The SB300 manual: 'Grip the door and shipper box along the vertical edge (pivot edge) with one hand and rotate the door until the wafer cushion contacts the wafers. Latch the lock on the pivot edge first... Apply inward pressure to the opposite side of the door until it is flush... and latch closed.' The cushion presses on 25 wafers, so the far side springs back until held flush, and the other hand must hold the door while the first latch turns. Tested: a set order, then a press held against a spring.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) A 300 mm wafer shipping box in the size of the Entegris SB300 (385 wide, 333 deep, 337 tall, published), clear polycarbonate, about 7 kg (estimate), standing on a 2 cm printed plate (the maker's three-pin kinematic coupling is not modelled: the box is held by friction, 1.2). Its opening faces the robot: the rim's front face is at x = 34, centred at y = 0. The opening is 34 wide and 25 tall, centred 20.4 cm above the bench; the rim is 1.2 cm deep. It holds 25 wafers, 300 mm across and 0.775 mm thick, 10 mm apart, the first 44 mm above the box's floor (published pitch), their front edges 1.8 cm behind the rim's face. The wafers are fixed in the box's shape. (2) The door: clear polycarbonate, 363.7 wide and 258.0 tall (published), 2.5 cm thick and 1.0 kg (estimates). Before closing it stands upright on a printed block (9 x 32 cm, 7.5 cm tall) in front of the box, held from tipping between two 3.5 cm tall, 8 mm thick printed rails 2.8 cm apart, its lower edge 7.5 cm above the bench, with its inner face at x = 28 and its centre 20.4 cm above the bench, centred at y = 0. On its inner face two spring pads, 2 x 2.5 cm, at y = +4.5 and -4.5, stand 3.3 cm proud and stand for the wafer cushion: each is a spring of 875 N/m, 14 N together at flush (estimate; the manual gives no force). (3) Two D-rings on the door's outer face at y = +15 and -15, mid-height: a 12 mm square bar, 5.2 cm long, on two 10 mm legs 4 cm apart, standing 4.2 cm proud of the face when lifted. They start lifted, with the bar upright. Each ring turns about its stem (a quarter turn, 90 degrees counter-clockwise seen from the robot latches it; the cam is set at 1 N m, an estimate; the manual's maximum is 4.4 N m, no typical value is published) and, after that, folds down onto the door. A latch counts as engaged only when its ring is turned 80 degrees or more while its side of the door is within 1 mm of flush on the box; an engaged latch holds its side to the rim with 12 N. Nothing else is on the bench. Run limit 3,000 steps (20 Hz). Real trial: an SB300 or any 300 mm FOSB with its own door and cushion. In place of the wafers, 25 discs of 5052 aluminium, 300 mm across and 0.81 mm (0.032 in) thick, 154 g (a wafer is 128 g; the scene uses no wafer mass), edges filed round, one in each slot against the back stops: the diameter puts each front edge where a wafer's is, so the box's own cushion meets them and gives the real closing resistance; they sag about twice as much as silicon, under 1 mm at the front edge. They are cut four to a 610 mm sheet, seven sheets for about 156 USD, and reused. The top disc's front edge is marked red. Also the printed plate and rest, a pencil outline of the box on the plate, a phone above the box and a printed protractor (on 1 mm card, its front 40 mm overhanging the rim face, 24 mm above the door's top edge) on its top. Cost: a new 12 inch FOSB 484.95 USD (MSE Supplies; new price) plus the discs 156 USD, snips 15 USD: about 660 USD in all (a used box, eBay item 355280761686 at 29.99 USD plus about 100 USD shipping, may have ended, would bring it near 300 USD). Before the first trial, read the box's cushion push at the right edge with a push-pull gauge (use a box under 20 N; the simulator's is 14 N, estimate range 10 to 18 N) and its cam torque with a luggage scale on the D-ring bar (use at most 1 N m, the simulator's value, 38 N at 26 mm; the manual's maximum is 4.4 N m), and write both in the README's Real column. Reset: unlatch both rings, lift them, set the door back upright on the block between its rails. Entegris and SB300 are trademarks of Entegris, Inc., named for identification only.
scoring: Terms: a latch is engaged when its ring is turned 80 degrees or more while its side is within 1 mm of flush (real trial: the cam turns home only on a seated door). A ring turned 30 degrees or more while its side is more than 2 mm from flush does not count until it is turned back to within 10 degrees of its start. Tiers: 0.25 the left latch engaged. 0.5 both. 0.75 also the door flush all round: a 0.5 mm feeler enters at none of the four corners (the same feeler on the real box). 1.0 also both D-rings folded 80 degrees or more (real: flat on the door), the cushion pressed on the wafers (sim: both pads 6 mm or more; real: the door flush with all 25 discs in, the cushion seen on them through the clear door), and both grippers 3 cm clear and the door still for 1 s (real: video). Zeros that stick: the box moves more than 5 mm on its plate (real: the pencil outline) or lifts off it for 0.5 s; the door drops; the right latch engages before the left (real: the latch order on video); the cushion first touches the wafers with the door more than 5 degrees out of square (sim: 1 mm of pad travel; real: an overhead phone at 60 frames a second, the door's top edge read against a printed protractor centred on the pivot corner, in the first frame the cushion meets the red-marked top disc). No tier depends on the cushion's force or the cam's torque.
reset_notes: Both D-rings unlatched and lifted, the door on its rest at x = 28, the box on its plate. No seed changes the scene; the jitter run shifts free parts by up to 1 cm.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz on GPU, rigid parts and sprung joints. Wafers fixed in the box (real: seated in slots, held by the cushion). The cushion is two spring pads, 14 N at flush; it, the 1 kg door and the 1 N m cam torque are estimates, each with its real check in the README. A latch is a rule: it engages when its ring is turned while its side is within 1 mm of flush, then holds that side with 12 N. The demo reads the door's pose; a policy sees cameras. Meshes are hand-built from published sizes.
scores: demo: 1.0 on 3 of 3 README runs (560 of 3,000 steps), 4 of 4 jittered runs and one run on a second GPU; Dream-1 run: 0.0 (3,000 steps)
